modules.behavior: Streaming CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE generator over a valid/ready byte stream with a frame-end flag. Algorithm: width 16, polynomial 0x1021, initial value 0xFFFF, input and output NOT reflected, no final XOR, each byte processed most-significant bit first. One byte update of state S with byte D: S = S ^ (D << 8), then 8 times S = S[15] ? ((S << 1) ^ 0x1021) : (S << 1), masked to 16 bits. Check value: the bytes 0x31..0x39 ('123456789') sent as one frame give 0x29B1 on the last byte. The module keeps a running frame state F, equal to 0xFFFF after reset. A byte is accepted at a rising clk edge exactly when in_valid && in_ready before that edge and rst is low. For each accepted byte let C = update(F, in_data): register out_crc = C, out_last = in_last and out_valid = 1, then set F = 0xFFFF if in_last = 1 (the next accepted byte starts a new frame), else F = C. So out_crc is the CRC of every byte of the current frame up to and including this byte, and the consumer takes the frame CRC from the output whose out_last = 1. Invalid or blocked bytes never change F or the output. One output slot, capacity 1: in_ready = !out_valid || out_ready, a combinational path from out_ready; out_valid is the slot state. At an edge with out_valid && out_ready and no accepted byte, out_valid clears; at an edge that both retires and accepts, the slot is replaced and out_valid stays 1, so one byte per cycle is sustained. No bypass: a byte captured at edge k is visible after edge k and can transfer at edge k+1 at the earliest (minimum accepted-transfer age 1). While out_valid && !out_ready, out_valid, out_crc and out_last stay stable. out_crc and out_last are unspecified while out_valid = 0. Synchronous active-high rst at a rising edge clears out_valid, discards the slot, restarts the frame (F = 0xFFFF) and overrides any capture. Reset has no effect between edges (an off-edge rst pulse changes nothing), and in_ready/out_valid reflect slot state even while rst is asserted: no combinational reset gating. Producers hold in_data, in_last and in_valid while blocked. For the Python scoreboard oracle ONLY: each non-reset step is one accepted byte; keep F in state, compute C, return out_crc = C and out_last = in_last, then advance F as above. A supplied rst returns F to 0xFFFF and outputs 0; init() is the reset state. Do not model the slot, readiness or backpressure in the oracle. Each example starts from reset and after_cycles repeats the same accepted byte.

objective_policy: First establish timing feasibility. A verified timing-feasible candidate may replace a known timing-infeasible previous best even with higher area or power; classify this as timing_recovery, not objective savings. While the previous best is timing-infeasible, a verified still-infeasible candidate with strictly better setup WNS and hold not worse beyond a small tolerance may replace it as timing_progress, which is not closure; a feasible candidate always outranks it. Once both are timing-feasible, require strict improvement of the chosen objective; for maximize_freq that is register-to-register setup slack (reg2reg_wns_ns) when both designs report it, otherwise full setup WNS for both, while feasibility stays on full WNS and WHS. minimize_luts compares (lut_used, ff_used) and minimize_ffs compares (ff_used, lut_used) lexicographically: an equal primary metric with a strictly lower secondary is an objective improvement, a higher primary never is, and a secondary missing from either design gives no tie-break. Unknown or contradictory incumbent timing evidence cannot establish recovery. A completed experiment may find no improvement. Do not invent mandatory savings, slack margins, tool versions, timing corners, new tests, thresholds, code-style quotas or external environment requirements.
